analyst_view.overall: Early view: Dinamo (9th, 7 points) were under interim coach Jerko Leko after parting with Mario Kovacevic at the start of November, yet won 2-0 at Sunderland in his first game; a permanent appointment could come before this. Leverkusen (7th, 9 points) lost their perfect European record at home to Marseille but beat Koln 2-1 in the Rhine derby before the break.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals. I lean lower: both sides' European games have averaged 2.25 goals, and Leverkusen have conceded once in four league-phase games even while leaking goals in the Bundesliga in October. Dinamo have kept clean sheets in both away games and were only really open in the 2-4 home loss to NEC, so 1-2 or 0-2 fits better than a high score.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners, most of them for Leverkusen. That fits: Leverkusen took more shots than anyone over the first three rounds and should have long spells of pressure at Maksimir, while Dinamo look to counter. I'd stay with around 10.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards. I lean a little higher: Dinamo defended deep and fouled a lot while protecting their lead at Sunderland, and they are likely to spend long periods without the ball again in front of a demanding home crowd. The referee has not been named.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.6 shots. Leverkusen were the competition's busiest shooters until a quiet night against Marseille, and Dinamo goalkeeper Dominik Kotarski had to make seven saves at Sunderland, so a Leverkusen-heavy total around the site's figure looks right.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.8 shots on target. Leverkusen's accuracy has swung from very high in the first three rounds to three on target against Marseille, and Dinamo rarely test goalkeepers away from their counters, so I stay with the number.
